title: BehaimITS resells Flowable licences while its primary platform allegiance is TIBCO
content:
The Flowable card for BehaimITS says it provides Flowable licensing, and the research reads that as reseller-leaning: the engine appears as something the firm can sell rather than something it builds practice around. Its primary platform allegiance is recorded as TIBCO.

Both halves of that matter for how directory membership should be interpreted. A licensing-only presence tells you the firm has a commercial arrangement, not that it has delivered anything; the flag's own hedge, "reseller-leaning", concedes that delivery depth is unevidenced. And an allegiance pointing at another platform vendor means the firm's incentives, references and staff specialisation sit somewhere other than the engine it is listed against.

Two disqualifiers therefore stack here — divided allegiance and a Chicago base outside the EU scope. The same divided-loyalty pattern recurs across the sweep: ERRY resells the competing Bonita engine, and EPAM and TCS hold Camunda tiers alongside their Flowable listings. In every case the firm is also excluded on geography or scale, so nothing in scope is being lost to this criterion alone.
